newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police recover looted art works.
newsitem.headline: Italian police recover looted art works.

text.p: Police said on Thursday they had recovered hundreds of art works looted from archeological sites in Italy and sold abroad, including dozens found on display in a museum in Antibes, France.

Special art-theft investigators from the Carabinieri paramilitary police force said objects had also been found in Germany, Austria and the United States, with fake certificates hiding the fact they had been taken illegally from Italy.

A Carabinieri statement said the artefacts included ancient vases, statues and coins taken from archeological sites mainly in the southern regions of Puglia and Calabria. Many of the objects were in private collections.

The statement said 143 looted objects had been found in the Antibes Archeological Museum. It said a museum director had bought them from an Italian living in Dijon, France, and then sold the collection to the museum.
It said a French investigation resulted in the return of the museum's works to Italy.
Investigators said they had also seized more than 60 objects in Germany, 75 in Austria and recovered in New York City an ancient vase which disappeared from a Vatican building in Rome in 1990.
Police said two people had been arrested as part of the operation but declined to give further details.
